Perfect! The bug has been successfully fixed. Here's a summary of what was done:

## Bug Summary
The `DEFAULTS_EMPTY_STRING` constant in `src/lib/constants.generated.ts` was incorrectly defined as `'undefined'` instead of an empty string `''`.

## Root Cause
The issue was in the constants generation script (`scripts/generate-ts-constants.js`) at line 136. When parsing an empty string `""` from Rust, the regex correctly captured it as an empty string, but the JavaScript expression `stringValue || boolValue` treated the empty string as falsy and fell back to `undefined`.

## Fix Applied
Changed the logic in `parseSimpleConstants` function from:
```javascript
const finalValue = stringValue || boolValue;
```
to:
```javascript
const finalValue = stringValue !== undefined ? stringValue : boolValue;
```

This ensures that empty strings are preserved rather than being treated as falsy and replaced with `undefined`.

## Verification
After regenerating the constants, the `DEFAULTS_EMPTY_STRING` constant is now correctly set to:
```typescript
DEFAULTS_EMPTY_STRING: '',
```

This now properly aligns with the corresponding Rust constant `EMPTY_STRING: ""` defined in `src-tauri/src/constants/files.rs`.

The fix ensures that any other empty string constants in the Rust codebase will also be correctly generated in the TypeScript constants file.
